title: Uniformly small nonzero flat subsheaves with flat quotient
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with tensor-flatness as in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For a module sheaf $M$ define its size by $|M|=|\coprod_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)}M(U)|$, the cardinality of the disjoint union of all its sets of sections. There is an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, depending only on the site and $R$, such that every nonzero flat module sheaf $F$ has a subobject $0\ne P\subseteq F$ with $|P|\le\kappa$, $P$ flat, and the sheaf quotient $F/P$ flat. All sets and cardinals are taken in a fixed universe containing the small site and the section sets of $R$. No enough-points or sectionwise-flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated bounded-subobject input for proof paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction. WANTED: Rene Recktenwald, Construction of Six Functor Formalisms (2019), Proposition 2.5.31, Lemmas 2.5.12 and 2.5.25, Corollary 1.4.7 and the proof of Corollary 2.5.33, printed pp. 73-76, https://d-nb.info/1211326829/34. Read online, not archived. No Stacks tag states this uniform bounded flat-subobject lemma.

proof.text: Choose an infinite cardinal $\lambda$ bounding the cardinalities of $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, $\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal C)$, and $\coprod_U R(U)$, and put $\kappa=2^\lambda$. These depend only on the ringed site and belong to the fixed universe. We use the elementary cardinal identities $\lambda\cdot\lambda=\lambda$, $\kappa\cdot\kappa=\kappa$, $\kappa^{<\omega}=\kappa$, and $\kappa^\lambda=(2^\lambda)^\lambda=2^{\lambda\times\lambda}=\kappa$. A family of arrows with fixed target has at most $\lambda$ distinct arrows; even if a covering repeats an arrow, restrictions of a given section on its repetitions coincide. Thus covering data for sections can be encoded by their target object, a subset of the set of arrows, and one section per distinct arrow, irrespective of the size of a covering's original index set.

source.place: Tag 00VH (definition-site); elementary cardinal arithmetic and encoding of restrictions by distinct arrows.

proof.text: For a family $S\subseteq\coprod_U F(U)$ with $|S|\leq\kappa$, define a subpresheaf $H_S\subseteq F$ as follows: $H_S(V)$ is the $R(V)$-span of all $s|_V$ for $(U,s)\in S$ and arrows $V\to U$. Restricting a finite linear combination restricts both its coefficients and its generators, so these are submodules stable under restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There are at most $\lambda|S|\leq\kappa$ restricted generators altogether, and each element of $H_S(V)$ is a finite linear combination with coefficients in $R(V)$. The elementary finite-tuple count therefore gives $|\coprod_V H_S(V)|\leq\kappa$.

source.place: Sections 03CS (presheaves of modules) and 03CV (sheaves of modules); explicit span and finite-tuple count.

proof.text: For any subpresheaf of modules $H\subseteq F$ of total section size at most $\kappa$, define $L(H)(U)$ to consist of those $s\in F(U)$ for which some covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has $s|_{U_i}\in H(U_i)$ for all $i$. Pulling back witnessing coverings proves restriction stability. Common refinements, obtained by pulling back one covering along the other, show closure under addition; scalar multiplication uses the same witnessing covering. A matching family of such sections glues uniquely in $F$, and composing its witnessing coverings shows that its glue lies in $L(H)$, so $L(H)$ is a subsheaf. It is the smallest subsheaf containing $H$, since a subsheaf containing $H$ contains every such local glue. Each of its sections is determined by the restrictions on a witnessing covering. By Step 1 these restrictions have a code consisting of the target object $U$, a subset of at most $\lambda$ arrows and at most $\lambda$ elements of $\coprod_VH(V)$. Choose one code for each section; two sections with the same code lie over the same object, agree on a witnessing covering, and hence are equal by separatedness of $F$. An empty witnessing covering contributes one empty restriction code for each target object, and separatedness still gives uniqueness over that object. Therefore $|L(H)|\leq\lambda\cdot 2^\lambda\cdot\kappa^\lambda=\kappa$. Write $B(S)=L(H_S)$. This constructs the subsheaf generated by $S$, proves $|B(S)|\leq\kappa$, and shows that every section of $B(S)$ is locally a finite linear combination of restrictions of members of $S$.

source.place: Tag 00VH (definition-site), composition and base change of coverings; the sheaf axiom. Agent local-saturation construction and explicit cardinal count.

proof.text: Since $F\ne0$, some $F(U)$ has a nonzero section $s$: otherwise every section group is zero and $F$ is the zero sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Set $N_0=B(\{(U,s)\})$. Suppose $N_j\subseteq F$ has been constructed with $|N_j|\leq\kappa$. For each object $V$, integers $r,t\geq0$, matrix $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{r\times t}(R(V))$, and vector $c\in N_j(V)^r$ such that $Ax=c$ has a solution $x\in F(V)^t$, choose one such solution. There are at most $\kappa$ systems: the object set and all ring sections have size at most $\lambda$, and all right-hand sides are finite tuples of the at most $\kappa$ sections of $N_j$. Let $S_j$ consist of all sections of $N_j$ and all entries of these chosen solutions. Then $|S_j|\leq\kappa$, and $N_{j+1}=B(S_j)$ contains $N_j$ and has size at most $\kappa$ by Steps 2-3. This is an ordinary countable recursion using choice over a set of nonempty solution sets, with no assumption that $F(V)$ is a flat $R(V)$-module.

source.place: Section 03CV: module operations on sections. Agent finite-linear-system closure, with the bounded-generation construction of Steps 2-3.

proof.text: Let $D(V)=\bigcup_{j<\omega}N_j(V)$. Because the $N_j$ increase, finite sums and scalar multiples remain in some $N_j(V)$, so $D\subseteq F$ is a subpresheaf of modules with $|D|\leq\aleph_0\kappa=\kappa$. Set $P=L(D)$. Step 3 proves that $P$ is a subsheaf with $|P|\leq\kappa$, and it contains the original nonzero section $s$. Moreover every finite tuple of sections of $P(V)$ locally belongs to a single $N_j$: choose a witnessing covering for each tuple entry, take their finite common refinement using the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and on each member take the maximum of the finitely many indices appearing there. The index may vary among members of the covering. This uses local membership in the union, and does not assert that a sectionwise countable union of subsheaves is already a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 00VH (definition-site); common refinements from covering base change and composition, followed by the construction of Step 3.

proof.text: We now have the following local reflection of finite systems. If $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{r\times t}(R(V))$, $c\in P(V)^r$, and $x\in F(V)^t$ satisfies $Ax=c$, apply Step 5 to the finite tuple $c$. On each resulting covering member $W\to V$, all entries of $c|_W$ lie in one $N_j(W)$. The restricted system, including its restricted matrix, has the actual solution $x|_W$ in $F(W)^t$. Consequently Step 4 selected a solution of that very system whose entries belong to $N_{j+1}(W)\subseteq P(W)$. Thus any finite system with right-hand side in $P$ which has a solution in $F$ has solutions in $P$ locally. We will use precisely this proved property, without introducing a purity notion or citing an uncited purity theorem.

source.place: Agent finite-linear-system argument from Steps 4-5; coefficients are restricted together with their equations.

proof.text: To prove that $P$ is flat, take a relation $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i p_i=0$ in $P(V)$, with $a_i\in R(V)$. It is a relation in $F(V)$, since $P(V)\subseteq F(V)$. By flatness of $F$ and [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion], there is a covering on whose members $W$ one has $p_i|_W=\sum_{q=1}^l b_{iq}z_q$, with $z_q\in F(W)$ and $\sum_i a_i|_W b_{iq}=0$. Regard these factorization equations as the finite system $Bz=(p_i|_W)_i$. Step 6 gives, after a further covering, a solution $z'_q\in P$ for the same restricted coefficient matrix $B$. The coefficient identities $\sum_i a_i b_{iq}=0$ restrict unchanged. Composing the coverings yields exactly the local factorization required by the converse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion]. Hence $P$ is tensor-flat. The case $n=0$ is included: the empty relation admits the empty factorization.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), equivalence (1) and (2), applied first to F and then to P; the finite-system reflection is Step 6.

proof.text: Let $Q=F/P$ be the cokernel sheaf. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] it is the sheafification of the presheaf $E(V)=F(V)/P(V)$. The module sheafification has underlying abelian sheaf the abelian sheafification by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], and its underlying set sheaf is the associated sheaf of the underlying sets by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] implies that every section of $Q$ locally comes from $E$ and hence locally lifts to $F$. It also implies that if $f\in F(V)$ maps to zero in $Q(V)$, then its class in $E(V)$ is locally zero: locally $f\in P$. Since $P$ is a subsheaf, those local restrictions glue inside $P$ to $f$, so already $f\in P(V)$. Finite tuples of sections of $Q$ admit simultaneous local lifts by successively refining the finitely many coverings. No sectionwise surjectivity of $F\to Q$ is claimed.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), the preceding description of cokernels; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules). Underlying sets and local representatives: Sites Tags 00WB (theorem-plus), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification).

proof.text: Take $a_i\in R(V)$ and $q_i\in Q(V)$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n a_iq_i=0$. Step 8 gives a covering on which the $q_i$ have simultaneous lifts $f_i\in F$. On each member, $c=\sum_i a_i f_i$ maps to zero in $Q$ and therefore belongs to $P$ by Step 8. The single equation $\sum_i a_i y_i=c$ has the solution $(f_i)_i$ in $F$, so Step 6 gives a solution $(y_i)_i$ in $P$ after a further covering. Then $g_i=f_i-y_i$ satisfies $\sum_i a_i g_i=0$ in $F$. By flatness of $F$ and [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion], after another covering $g_i=\sum_q b_{iq}t_q$ with $\sum_i a_i b_{iq}=0$. Passing to $Q$ gives $q_i=\sum_q b_{iq}\overline{t_q}$ because each $y_i$ maps to zero. These are the required factorizations for $Q$, and composition of the successive coverings is a covering. The converse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-equational-criterion] now shows that $Q$ is tensor-flat. Empty relations are handled by the empty factorization as in Step 7. Together with Steps 1 and 5 and the flatness of $P$ from Step 7, this proves all clauses with the single uniform bound $\kappa=2^\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), equivalence (1) and (2); quotient lifts and kernel membership from Step 8, finite-system reflection from Step 6. Tag 00VH for composite coverings.
